payload.text: hv, 10 Nov, relayed verbatim by utilz-dc from hv's first-hand word in dc's own window, received by vc's date -u of 11:16Z: "write the driver for exec_create_space before the cut." NOT first-hand in vc's session, and recorded as a relay so the provenance is not misread; hv can correct it. It answered the question dc put to hv, which is the one the green left open and which dc framed better than vc had: hv's ruling of this morning has two clauses, the arms' green answers "C5B9WJ is green" in substance through NTVCDH, and it does NOT answer "don't ship it unrun" for arngz.lua's engine, because the arms cannot reach exec_create_space at all and that unrun function -- four commits with a defect found after each by a reader, no suite coverage and no live proof -- is the very code dc's report was about when hv ruled. SO THIS ANSWERS THE OPEN TEST-SURFACE QUESTION, in the direction of building a surface: the question leaves intent/wip.md as hv's, because hv has now called it. It adds a second condition before the cut rather than superseding anything: decision 96's gate stands, the arms are green, and the cut now also waits on a driver that does not exist yet. OWNER, named by vc so that two sessions do not write the same thing as nearly happened with acceptance.sh today: utilz-dc owns and writes it. It is a test surface, which is devx work rather than validation work; vc writing ST0032's code at all was the departure recorded in decision 95 only because dc was down, and dc is up; and vc owes ST0032's acceptance contract. vc checks the driver by change and by reading, which restores vc's advisory role on this thread. WHERE IT LANDS: a NEW steel thread, dc's lean and vc's agreement, related to ST0032 with `intent st relate` so each is findable from the other. A WP on ST0032 would gate the cut on a thread whose contract vc is still writing and would mix a proof surface with three defect fixes and a feature; hv's question stood on wip.md as new scope and hv's call, so it lands as new scope now that hv has called it. THE SHAPE, dc's and endorsed by vc: an INJECTED `hs`, not Hammerspoon. A scripted fake for hs.spaces so the driver runs under plain lua as plan_test.lua does, with no Hammerspoon, no pointer, no Mac and no desk booking, which leaves dc's watch-out 3 untouched and puts it inside `utilz test` and CI. The reason it is proof rather than ceremony is the thread's own distillation, that the arithmetic was never wrong and what was wrong every time was the function's account of what it had done: an injected hs makes all four reporting paths deterministic, including the two a real machine cannot produce to order, the readback that lags after a creation and the overshoot where the desktops go from n to n+2. A live run can reach neither on purpose, which is why four commits of reading never caught them. VC'S CONDITION ON ITS CHECK: every arm proven by MUTATION, one at a time, with the one-line change to arngz.lua named in the record and reverted after, because an arm written against working code can pass while asserting nothing and critic-shell found three of vc's own tests in that state today, one of which could not go red at all. The four that matter: the final-failure path not consulting `made`; a creating call retried on a lagging count; the overshoot undetected; and the vanished display retried rather than stopped. An arm that cannot be made to go red is not an arm. AND THE THING THAT WOULD CHANGE THE DESIGN, which dc is reading now: whether `hs` is reachable as a global at call time or captured at load, which decides whether arngz.lua can be loaded under plain lua at all. If it cannot, arngz.lua is NOT to be bent to suit the driver without telling vc first: a source edit moves the tree out from under the ancestry check dc itself added, voids the green at 5d7bfe37 and needs a fresh run, so it is a finding and a decision rather than a step. Peers read this decision at pickup; dc owns the new thread and records no copy of the decision.
